# Free third-party material

Code and files from other projects that are free software, the kind Debian main takes. XeStrata may build and run
with them. Each project's folder keeps its own license text.

| Folder | Project | License | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ggml/` | [ggml / llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | MIT (`ggml/LICENSE`) | `ggml-common.h`, an unmodified copy at the commit in `ggml/VERSION.txt` (it stays MIT): the block layouts and codebook grids of the quantized formats. Needed to build the engine. Update it only together with the pinned llama.cpp (the engine also links ggml-cpu from it) |
| `ggml-tq/` | [agentionai/llama.cpp](https://github.com/agentionai/llama.cpp), a fork of llama.cpp, as upstream Strata copied it | MIT (`ggml-tq/LICENSE`) | `ggml-common-tq.h`, unmodified from upstream Strata's `third_party/ggml/ggml-common-tq.h` (it stays MIT): the block layouts and the 2048-point codebook of the trellis expert formats TQ2_T, TQK6 and TQK7 (agentionai's Gyro models). The CPU's and the GPU's trellis kernels read it. Needed to build the engine |
| `intel-llvm/` | [intel/llvm](https://github.com/intel/llvm) (DPC++) | Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions (`intel-llvm/LICENSE.TXT`) | Not the compiler itself, which `tools/intel_llvm_build.py` clones from intel/llvm at the release it pins (v7.1.1) and builds into `.tools/`: XeStrata's fixes to it, `patches/NN-<id>.patch`, which the script applies in order before building. They are under intel/llvm's license, as changes to its files; each says what it fixes. The deb and rpm packages carry the SYCL runtime of the intel/llvm built so (`libsycl`, UR's loader and adapters, `libumf`), with this license text |
| `rocm-device-libs/` | [ROCm's device libraries](https://github.com/ROCm/llvm-project/tree/rocm-7.2.4/amd/device-libs) (ocml, ockl and the others), by AMD | University of Illinois/NCSA (`rocm-device-libs/LICENSE.TXT`) | Not the libraries themselves, which `tools/intel_llvm_build.py` clones from ROCm's llvm-project at the release it pins (`rocm-7.2.4`, on the same LLVM as the intel/llvm it builds) and builds with intel/llvm into `.tools/`, with the target features Debian's rocm-llvm package gives their build (transcribed from its `debian/rules`, Expat: see NOTICE); without them CMake takes a ROCm's device libraries the compiler reads (`cmake/StrataHip.cmake`). The AMD code links them: the engine's kernels for AMD GPUs carry parts of them, so the deb and rpm packages carry this license text |
| `llama.cpp/` | [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | MIT (its own `LICENSE`) | Not in the repository: setup fetches it at the pinned commit. ggml-cpu for the CPU experts, the image encoder's `mtmd`, and `gguf-py` for the tools. The deb and rpm packages carry `gguf-py` with llama.cpp's `LICENSE` |
| `oneMath/` | [oneMath](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneMath) | Apache-2.0 (`oneMath/LICENSE`) | Not oneMath itself, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches from XeStrata's fork ([MistVVK/oneMath](https://github.com/MistVVK/oneMath), branch `xestrata`) at the tag it pins (`xestrata-3`, its archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_ONEMATH_SOURCE` (a local archive or URL); in the contrib-llvm and contrib-icpx modes, and in the free mode for AMD GPUs. The fork is oneMath's commit 6ff3a43 with XeStrata's changes as commits and oneMath's `develop` merged into it (up to 1308c5e), under oneMath's license, each marking the files it changes in their headers: the cuBLAS backend's BF16 product (oneMath has none), and the rocBLAS backend's 16-bit products through hipBLASLt where it has kernels for the GPU (ROCm 7.1's rocBLAS has no tuned ones for RDNA4), the cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends' SYCL targets on their own libraries, so that one build makes both, and the rocBLAS backend without what HIP and SYCL deprecate (HIP's context API, the comparisons with `HIP_SUCCESS`, `get_access` for a host accessor). On Windows `CMakeLists.txt` also applies `oneMath/patches/windows-gnu-driver.patch` to the fetched tree until the fork carries it (oneMath with a GNU-style SYCL driver, intel/llvm's clang++; its rocBLAS backend on Windows; the backend's function table exported from its DLL), under oneMath's license. oneMath runs the dense matrix products through its oneMKL (Intel), cuBLAS (NVIDIA) and rocBLAS (AMD) backends. The deb and rpm packages carry the oneMath built so (its rocBLAS backend; the contrib-llvm ones its oneMKL and cuBLAS backends too), with this license text |
| `quantscope/` | [quantscope](https://github.com/1872183316/quantscope) | MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option (`quantscope/LICENSE-MIT`, `quantscope/LICENSE-APACHE`) | `quantscope.py`, unmodified at commit bfdf205 but for a line saying where it comes from (as upstream Strata took it, #911): it reads a GGUF's headers only (a file, a folder, a URL, a ModelScope or Hugging Face repository). `tools/strata_inspect.py` and `setup.py --inspect` use it to say what a GGUF really is and whether XeStrata runs it. Without it only that check is gone |
| `stb/` | [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) | MIT or public domain (the Unlicense), at your option (`stb/LICENSE`, the header's own end) | `stb_image.h` v2.30, unmodified (the copy llama.cpp carries in `vendor/stb`): the image engine (`strata-image`) reads an edit's reference image with it (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF). Needed to build the image engine |
| `outfit/` | [Outfit](https://github.com/Outfitio/Outfit-Fonts) | SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`outfit/OFL.txt`) | The web app's font (WOFF2, Latin and Latin Extended). Without it the web app uses the system font |
